messages:
Anya - Support: @here customer Jonas (acct) reporting sustained 429s for EU traffic starting ~09:12 UTC. They say token-level errors show 'rate_limit_exceeded' even though their dashboard shows quota left. Can we triage?

Jonas (acct): I'm seeing about 4-6% of requests get 429s. Headers show region=eu-west-1 in request but responses sometimes served from us-east-1. We didn't change anything on our side.

Sam W: thanks, Anya. quick Q: are the 429s 'quota_exhausted' or 'burst_credit_exhausted' in the response body? can you paste a raw response?

Jonas (acct): here is one (redacted):

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
content-type: application/json
x-redwood-region: us-east-1
x-rate-limit-retry-after: 3
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "detail": "burst credits exhausted for tenant",
  "quota_remaining": 0
}
```

Liam (SRE): interesting that x-redwood-region is us-east-1 while request was eu-west-1. That implies regional failover/routing kicked in. Could be EU capacity saturated and requests fell back to us cluster where tenant had no burst credits left.

Anya - Support: Customer insists their dedicated EU pool is fine — they have a Dedicated plan. Could this be cross-zone spill due to autoscaler not spinning up fast enough?

Sam W: possible. Two lines to check: 1) routing decision log for that tenant at the time (should show region selection + fallback reason). 2) tenant-level burst credit consumption across regions. Liam, can you pull those counters?

Liam (SRE): grabbing logs now. initial grep: `router:decision tenant=jonas-co region=eu-west-1 result=fallback target=us-east-1 reason=capacity-pressure span_ms=12`
Also: `quota:burst tenant=jonas-co used=1250 allocated=1000 window=60s status=exhausted`

Liam (SRE): seems they blew through burst credits in the minute when traffic spiked. Router then fell back to us-east where their burst remaining was 0, causing 429s downstream.

Anya - Support: Jonas — can you share your traffic pattern? Is it spiky?

Jonas (acct): past 2 deploys caused short spikes ~6k rps for 30s; normally ~600 rps steady. We rely on burst to handle deploy-time syncs.

Sam W: ok that matches. Two parallel remediation paths: short-term — top up burst credits and/or route them to an EU emergency pool. Long-term — bump their dedicated EU capacity or adjust autoscale thresholds and pre-warm. Which do we want?

BillingBot: note — we can issue a one-time burst credit top-up for this tenant up to 10k tokens for emergency; requires approval from billing lead.

Anya - Support: I'll ask for approval. Meanwhile, Liam can we add a routing rule to prefer eu-west-1 and avoid spilling to us-east if EU fallback would cause auth/billing mismatch? Maybe fallback to 'cache-only' or queue.

Liam (SRE): we have a soft guard: if fallback target has zero burst and would return 429, router can prefer returning 429 early with `x-fallback-block` to avoid cross-region auth surprises. But that would still be 429s — slightly different semantics. I can push a temporary policy that holds requests in short queue for 500ms to allow autoscaler.

Sam W: please do both: policy change (short queue) + create an emergency route to eu-warm pool if available. Liam, how quickly can you make the router policy change?

Liam (SRE): I can roll a feature flag for the short-hold policy now and enable for tenant jonas-co. DeployBot will show progress.

DeployBot: started rollout for flag `router.short_hold_on_capacity_pressure` target=jonas-co initiator=Liam (SRE).

Liam (SRE): flag enabled for jonas-co. Also created a temporary route override to eu-warm-pool-2.

Anya - Support: Billing lead approved temporary credit top-up. BillingBot — can you apply +5000 burst credits and confirm?

BillingBot: applied one-time burst_credit_topup tenant=jonas-co amount=5000 reason="emergency spike" initiated_by=Anya. New burst_pool=6000.

Jonas (acct): confirmed reduced 429s almost immediately. Still seeing occasional 429s (~0.2%) during the worst seconds but way better. Thanks.

Sam W: follow-ups: (1) recommend tenant to either increase reserved EU capacity or configure pre-warm on deploy. (2) Product/Docs: clarify that dedicated pools do not auto-appear infinitely during short spikes — burst credits are global and can be exhausted. (3) Engineering: consider changing router behavior to prefer local queuing vs cross-region fallback when target burst==0.

Anya - Support: I'll send the customer a summary and suggested remediation steps + link to docs. Jonas, also share your deploy cadence and we can propose a pre-warm script snippet.

Jonas (acct): will do. Thanks everyone.

Liam (SRE): logging action items here: `SRE-1023` check autoscaler cold-start time for eu-warm-pool-2, `SRE-1024` evaluate router fallback heuristics, `SRE-1025` add tenant burst dashboards to alerting.

Sam W: closing the customer incident once Jonas confirms stable for 24h. leaving this thread open for internal actions. :+1:
